places.name: Cádiz
past: The lords built their castle on the hill above the town, where it could watch the roads for leagues.
Founded in Roman times about a forum. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 69% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread.
7 houses were pulled down to make way for the wall.
Besieged; the suburbs outside the gates were burned to deny the enemy cover, and grew back after the peace.

The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 77% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; 2 stretches of the old wall inside were pulled down for a street along their line.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 50 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the western side; 21 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
The old tower keep was rebuilt as a great castle on the same ground.
The parish church was pulled down and rebuilt on its own ground as a great minster.

places.name: Vadonogal
past: The bishop's cathedral and its burg stood on the dry rise; below, the count founded a merchants' town on the waterfront. For a generation they had two councils, then one. Canals — fleets — were dug from the harbour into the merchant quarter, so that lighters could unload at the warehouse doors.
Walled.
A great fire burned 12 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.
A great fire burned 26 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Torrehierro
past: Farms and an alehouse about a green where the roads meet; a weekly market was granted in its second age.
3 houses were pulled down to make way for the wall.
Walled.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.
The Austin friars were given ground by the wall for their friary.
Besieged; the suburbs outside the gates were burned to deny the enemy cover, and grew back after the peace.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 31 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the eastern side; 17 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
A great fire burned 19 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Cerro Oro
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 87% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread.
A great fire burned 8 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The keep was enlarged into a castle of stone.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 95% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; a stretch of the old wall inside was pulled down for a street along its line.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 16 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
